es: Redactar un llamado persuasivo con gancho, problema, evidencia, énfasis y una petición clara para una causa local.

vocabulary.es: gancho: frase que atrapa al empezar

teaching.en: Imagine a vacant lot turning into a garden full of life: a good hook lets the audience see the result before you explain it.
teaching.es: Imagina un solar vacío convirtiéndose en un jardín lleno de vida: un buen gancho deja que el público vea el resultado antes de que lo expliques.
teaching.explanationEs: Hook: abre con una imagen o una pregunta que atrape; el solar vacío es la imagen.
segments: Imagine a vacant lot turning into a garden full of life: a
good hook lets the audience see the result before you explain it.
teaching.audioText: Imagine a vacant lot turning into a garden full of life: a good hook lets the audience see the result before you explain it.

teaching.en: Right now this lot grows litter, not vegetables, and placing the problem beside the dream is the quickest way to make people care.
teaching.es: Ahora mismo este solar produce basura, no verduras, y poner el problema junto al sueño es la forma más rápida de que a la gente le importe.
teaching.explanationEs: Problema con contraste: lo que hay frente a lo que podría haber.
segments: Right now this lot grows litter, not vegetables, and placing the problem
beside the dream is the quickest way to make people care.
teaching.audioText: Right now this lot grows litter, not vegetables, and placing the problem beside the dream is the quickest way to make people care.

teaching.en: To make a compelling case, add a figure and its source: according to our survey, one hundred and twenty families would visit the garden weekly.
teaching.es: Para presentar un argumento convincente, añade una cifra y su fuente: según nuestra encuesta, ciento veinte familias visitarían el huerto cada semana.
teaching.explanationEs: Evidencia honesta: dato concreto con fuente; according to introduce la fuente.
segments: To make a compelling case, add a figure and its source: according to
our survey, one hundred and twenty families would visit the garden weekly.
teaching.audioText: To make a compelling case, add a figure and its source: according to our survey, one hundred and twenty families would visit the garden weekly.

teaching.en: What we are asking for is not a fortune: with a tight budget, a few tools and your signature, the work can start this month.
teaching.es: Lo que pedimos no es una fortuna: con un presupuesto ajustado, unas pocas herramientas y tu firma, el trabajo puede empezar este mes.
teaching.explanationEs: Cleft con what: destaca lo que pides y hace que la petición parezca pequeña, no una fortuna.
segments: What we are asking for is not a fortune: with a tight budget,
a few tools and your signature, the work can start this month.
teaching.audioText: What we are asking for is not a fortune: with a tight budget, a few tools and your signature, the work can start this month.

teaching.en: Never before has this neighbourhood had such a chance to grow together, and never before have so many families offered to help.
teaching.es: Nunca antes había tenido este barrio una oportunidad así de crecer unido, y nunca antes se habían ofrecido tantas familias a ayudar.
teaching.explanationEs: Never before + auxiliar + sujeto: inversión para dar énfasis a la idea clave.
segments: Never before has this neighbourhood had such a chance to grow
together, and never before have so many families offered to help.
teaching.audioText: Never before has this neighbourhood had such a chance to grow together, and never before have so many families offered to help.

teaching.en: To rally support, end with one clear request: sign the petition today, and next summer we will share the first harvest together.
teaching.es: Para reunir apoyos, termina con una petición clara: firma la petición hoy y el próximo verano compartiremos juntos la primera cosecha.
teaching.explanationEs: Petición final: una sola acción concreta, con una razón para hacerla hoy.
segments: To rally support, end with one clear request: sign the petition
today, and next summer we will share the first harvest together.
teaching.audioText: To rally support, end with one clear request: sign the petition today, and next summer we will share the first harvest together.

prompt.es: Elige el mejor gancho para abrir el llamado de Sara.

choices.text: Who will speak for the vacant lot when nobody else remembers it?
Last year, cleaning the lot behind the school cost the council a great deal.
Imagine walking past the vacant lot and finding rows of green leaves instead of litter.

feedback.es: Un gancho eficaz hace ver una escena concreta: el solar con hojas verdes en lugar de basura. La pregunta y el dato no muestran el resultado.

hint.es: Busca la opción que hace imaginar una escena en vez de presentar el tema.

origin.text: Sara has two minutes at the neighbourhood meeting. Her topic is a garden for the vacant lot behind the school. She wants a first sentence that makes the audience picture the result before she asks for anything.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Lo que necesitamos es un presupuesto ajustado y tu firma.»

answer.text: What we need is a tight budget and your signature

feedback.es: El cleft con what coloca al final lo que se pide: what we need is + la petición.

hint.es: Empieza con What we need y sigue con is.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si firmas la petición hoy, empezaremos a plantar en mayo.»

feedback.es: Sign the petition es la colocación para «firmar una petición»; tras if en un condicional de futuro va el presente, no will.

hint.es: Tras «if» se usa presente simple, y el verbo es el que se hace con una firma.

origin.text: The council has agreed to lend the land. All that is missing is the support of the neighbourhood: if you ___ the petition today, we will start planting in May.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su función en el llamado.

pairs: Imagine a vacant lot turning green.
Only four of our thirty streets have a single tree.
What we need is a few Saturdays, not a fortune.

pairs.es: énfasis: destaca lo que se pide

pairs: Sign the petition at the school door today.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple un paso distinto: abrir, plantear el problema, destacar lo pedido y cerrar con una acción.

pairs.es: énfasis: destaca lo que se pide

pairs: Sign the petition at the school door today.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que equilibra mejor la evidencia y la emoción.

choices.text: Forty families signed up last month, and every signature is a child who wants to plant a seed.
Forty families signed up last month, which proves clearly that our whole neighbourhood is ready for a garden.
Forty families signed up last month, so those of you who have not signed yet will soon regret it bitterly.

feedback.es: Une la cifra (forty families) con un toque humano (a child who wants to plant a seed); la segunda solo da el dato y la tercera amenaza.

origin.text: Sara wants one sentence about the forty families who signed up last month. It must contain the figure and a personal touch, but it must not scare anyone.

prompt.es: Escucha el llamado y elige cómo está estructurado.

choices.text: It opens with a hook and some evidence but leaves the request too vague.
It opens with a hook, gives evidence and ends with one clear request.
It opens with a question, then lists the tools without giving any evidence.

feedback.es: Tiene gancho (la imagen), evidencia (forty families, thirty more) y una petición concreta con fecha (sign the petition before Friday).

origin.audio: Imagine a lot full of vegetables instead of litter. Last month, forty families asked us for a garden, and this month thirty more have joined them. We do not need a fortune; we need a few tools, a tight budget and your signature. Please sign the petition before Friday, and next summer we will share the harvest.

prompt.es: Lee el borrador. ¿Qué mejora necesita con más urgencia el párrafo?

choices.text: It needs a sharper hook, because the opening does not make us see anything.
It needs a clearer deadline, because the request does not say when to sign.
It needs evidence, such as a figure from a survey, to support its claims.

feedback.es: Tiene gancho y una petición con fecha, pero afirma que el huerto es bueno sin ninguna prueba: lo que más necesita es un dato concreto con su fuente.

origin.text: Draft paragraph: “Imagine our children playing among the vegetables: what a great garden it would be! Gardens make everyone happy, and everybody knows it, so there is no need to explain why. Please sign the petition at the school door before Friday.”

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nunca antes había significado tanto un pequeño solar para nosotros.»

answer.text: Never before has a small lot meant so much to us

feedback.es: Con never before al inicio, has va antes del sujeto a small lot y luego el participio meant.

prompt.es: Redacta el llamado de unas 150 palabras con la ficha de datos.

answer.text: Imagine a vacant lot turning into a garden full of life. Right now, it grows litter, not vegetables. According to our survey, 120 families would visit it weekly, and every one of them wants to help. What we need is a tight budget, a few tools and forty volunteers. Never before has our neighbourhood had such a chance to grow together. Who will plant the first seed if we do not? It is our children who will eat the vegetables, and it is our neighbours who will share the harvest. Some people see an empty lot; we see a garden. We are not asking for a fortune; we are asking for a few Saturdays. Every signature is a neighbour who is ready to help, and together we can rally support for this garden. So please do not wait. Sign the petition at the school door before Friday, and next summer we will share the first harvest together.
accepted: Imagine a vacant lot turning into a garden full of life. Right now, it grows litter, not vegetables. According to our survey, 120 families would visit it weekly, and every one of them wants to help. What we need is a tight budget, a few tools and forty volunteers. Never before has our neighbourhood had such a chance to grow together. Who will plant the first seed if we do not? It is our children who will eat the vegetables, and it is our neighbours who will share the harvest. Some people see an empty lot; we see a garden. We are not asking for a fortune; we are asking for a few Saturdays. Every signature is a neighbour who is ready to help, and together we can rally support for this garden. So please do not wait. Sign the petition at the school door before Friday, and next summer we will share the first harvest together.

Imagine a vacant lot full of vegetables instead of litter. According to our survey, 120 families would visit a garden weekly, and forty of them have already offered to help. What we need is a tight budget, a few tools and forty volunteers. Never before has our neighbourhood had such a chance to grow together. Who will plant the first seed if we do not? Some people see a vacant lot; we see a harvest. It is our children who will learn here, and it is our neighbours who will care for it. We are not asking for a fortune; we are asking for a few Saturdays. Please sign the petition at the school door before Friday, and next summer we will share the harvest together.

feedback.es: El llamado completo lleva gancho, dato de la encuesta, recursos de énfasis, los 40 voluntarios y la petición con fecha.

origin.text: Ficha: huerto comunitario en el solar vacío detrás de la escuela. Hoy solo hay basura. 120 familias respondieron una encuesta y lo visitarían cada semana. Se necesitan 40 voluntarios y herramientas, con un presupuesto ajustado. La petición se firma en la puerta de la escuela antes del viernes. Incluye gancho, dato, tres recursos de énfasis y una petición clara.

evidenceGroups: what we are asking for is

prompt.es: Completa: «Para reunir apoyos, Sara recoge firmas a la puerta de la escuela.»

feedback.es: Rally support es la colocación para reunir apoyos alrededor de una causa; en el contexto, las firmas son ese apoyo.

origin.text: The council will not move without pressure from the neighbourhood. To ___ support for the garden, Sara is collecting signatures at the school door every afternoon this week.

prompt.es: Escucha el cierre y elige qué busca la oradora con las dos últimas preguntas.

choices.text: To push the audience to act without waiting for the council alone.
To pressure the council into promising a budget before the month of June.
To show the council that the audience no longer trusts its promises.

feedback.es: Las preguntas retóricas finales invitan a actuar ya («Will you be the first to sign?»): la oradora no quiere esperar solo al ayuntamiento.

origin.audio: Nobody wanted to live next to an empty lot. Now forty families are asking for a garden, and the council has said it would like to help, although it cannot promise a budget before June. Some of you have told me you are too busy, and I understand that; but nobody here has less time than the children who are waiting. If we wait for the council alone, the land will stay empty for another year. So I will ask you one thing tonight: will you help them? Will you be the first to sign?

prompt.es: Completa: «Son los vecinos quienes cuidarán el huerto cada fin de semana.»

feedback.es: En el it-cleft, el sujeto destacado va seguido de who (personas) o that.

origin.text: The council will lend the land, but it will not water the beans. It is the neighbours ___ will look after the garden every weekend, and it is they who deserve the first harvest.

prompt.es: Elige con qué propósito dice la oradora esta frase.

choices.text: To admit that the project will not work unless much more money is found.
To make the request seem small enough for anyone to accept.
To suggest that the volunteers will be paid for their time.

feedback.es: Al contrastar «a fortune» con «a few Saturdays», la oradora hace que la petición parezca pequeña y fácil de conceder.

origin.text: “We are not asking for a fortune; we are asking for a few Saturdays.” The speaker says this just before she asks the audience to sign the petition.
